alt_text: The Cueva del Chileno rock shelter in southwestern Bolivia.
caption: Cueva del Chileno, a rock shelter in the Lipez Altiplano of southwestern Bolivia. The high-altitude setting is central to the interpretation because the detected psychoactive plants were not local to the immediate environment.
credit: Photo courtesy of Juan V. Albarracin-Jordan and Jose M. Capriles, via UC Berkeley News / PNAS release materials.

alt_text: The Cueva del Chileno ritual bundle with leather bag, snuffing tablets, tube, pouch, spatulas, textile, and plant remains.
caption: Contents of the Cueva del Chileno ritual bundle: leather bag, carved wooden snuffing tablets, snuffing tube with human-hair braids, fox-snout pouch, camelid-bone spatulas, dried plant material, and polychrome textile. The kit links chemical residues to a concrete technology of preparation and ingestion.
credit: Photos courtesy of Juan V. Albarracin-Jordan and Jose M. Capriles, via UC Berkeley News.

alt_text: Animal-skin pouch constructed from three fox snouts.
caption: Fox-snout pouch from the ritual bundle. Scrapings from the pouch interior yielded cocaine, benzoylecgonine, bufotenine, harmine, DMT, and a possible psilocin signal in the 2019 LC-MS/MS study.
credit: Photo courtesy of Juan V. Albarracin-Jordan and Jose M. Capriles, via UC Berkeley News; Penn State release credit: Jose Capriles, Penn State.
